nodes.name: Ru@Mn₃O₄ synthesis
nodes.procedure: The Ru@Mn₃O₄ hybrid hydrogel blocks were synthesized via a simple wet-chemical process (details in Supporting Information), with a post-treatment at 60°C for 12 h. Finally, Ru@Mn₃O₄ was obtained by freeze-drying method.

nodes.source_text: The Ru@Mn₃O₄ hybrid hydrogel blocks were synthesized via a simple wet-chemical process, with a post-treatment at 60°C for 12 h. Finally, Ru@Mn₃O₄ was obtained by freeze-drying method (Figure S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows morphology of Ru@Mn₃O₄ similar to pure Mn₃O₄; ultrafine Ru clusters (1.4 nm) decorated on Mn₃O₄ support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of Ru@Mn₃O₄ is similar with the pure Mn₃O₄ (Figures 1a and S2). Ultrafine Ru clusters are decorated on the Mn₃O₄ support

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacing of 0.22 nm matching Ru(002) and 0.26 nm for Mn₃O₄(103), smaller than pure Mn₃O₄ (0.27 nm), indicating lattice contraction due to strong MSI.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The measured lattice spacing (0.22 nm) matches well with the (002) facet of Ru... The interplanar spacing of 0.26 nm is assigned to the (103) crystal plane of Mn₃O₄, which is smaller than the corresponding spacing of pure Mn₃O₄ (0.27 nm)

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and EDS mapping confirm uniform distribution of O, Mn, and Ru elements in Ru@Mn₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark field-scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) image and EDS mapping of Ru@Mn₃O₄ indicate the uniform distributions of O, Mn, and Ru elements

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows only Mn₃O₄ peaks (JCPDS: 24-0734) for Ru@Mn₃O₄; Ru peaks absent due to low loading (7.2 wt%) and small cluster size; peaks shift to higher angles vs pure Mn₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: there are only diffraction signals of Mn₃O₄ for the Ru@Mn₃O₄ composite (JCPDS: 24-0734). The absence of characteristic peaks of Ru can be due to the low loading content and small cluster size... the characteristic XRD peaks of Ru@Mn₃O₄ shift to higher angles

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru content in Ru@Mn₃O₄ is 7.2 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma (ICPMS) measurements confirm that Ru content in Ru@Mn₃O₄ is only 7.2 wt% (Table S1)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru 3p peaks at 462.9/485.1 eV (Ru⁰, +0.5 eV shift) and new Ru-O peaks at 465.2/487.7 eV; O 1s new Ru-O-Mn peak at 529.8 eV; Mn 3p negative shift of 0.19 eV indicate electron transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the binding energy from Ru@Mn₃O₄ presents a positive shift of 0.5 eV... two new peaks at 465.2 and 487.7 eV appear... ascribed to the Ru-O bond... a new peak at 529.8 eV for Ru@Mn₃O₄ could be ascribed to the interfacial Ru-O-Mn bonds

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES confirms electron transfer from Ru to Mn₃O₄; Ru K-edge FT-EXAFS shows Ru-Ru at 2.68 Å and Ru-O-Mn at 2.02 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1g shows electron transfer from Ru to Mn₃O₄... The extended X-ray adsorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra (Figure 1h) show that Mn₃O₄ holds a dominant Ru-Ru coordination (2.68Å) and minor Ru-O-Mn coordination (2.02Å)

nodes.characterization_summary: New peak at 503.6 cm⁻¹ confirms Ru-O-Mn bonds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This point is also confirmed by Raman spectroscopy with the newly emerged peak at 503.6 cm⁻¹ in Ru@Mn₃O₄

nodes.characterization_summary: In 1.0 M KOH, adsorbed OH* peak (716 cm⁻¹) intensity decreases at potentials < -0.2 V vs slight increase on pure Mn₃O₄ and Ru NPs, indicating dynamic OH* desorption via heterojunction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: for Ru@Mn₃O₄, the Raman intensity of the adsorbed OH* (716 cm⁻¹) presents a slight increase with lowering potential from 0 to -0.2 V. However, when the potential is negative than -0.2 V, the intensity rapidly decreases
